decisive_items: Multiple cystic lesions within pancreatic head
1.9 × 1.7-cm mass in portal vein with extension to superior mesenteric vein
response.rationale: The pancreatic head mass with vascular extension and elevated CA19-9, combined with extreme lipase elevation and ghost-cell fat necrosis/polyarthritis, best fits pancreatic cancer causing paraneoplastic pancreatic panniculitis. Panniculitis is the cutaneous manifestation; isolated fat necrosis or panniculitis labels do not account for the pancreatic imaging/malignancy.

rejected.why: Negative RF/CCP and ghost-cell fat necrosis argue against rheumatoid arthritis.
No trauma history; fat necrosis is enzymatic/pancreatic, not traumatic.
Fat necrosis is a histologic component of the panniculitis, not the unifying pancreatic diagnosis.
Fistula is duct-vascular, not pleuropulmonary, and no pleural disease is described.
No supportive clinical or histologic features of erythema induratum.
Negative autoimmune work-up and ghost-cell fat necrosis are not consistent with vasculitis.
No acute abdominal pain/necrotizing pancreatitis syndrome; imaging suggests mass/vascular involvement.
No lipid derangement is provided; lipase/amylase excess is secondary to pancreatic pathology.
